title: Zombieproof Medical
subtitle: How to Keep the Living Living
review_status: AI-assisted educational text. Not independently clinically reviewed.

parts.title: Please Remain Among the Living
parts.blurb: A safer scene, a useful order, and enough help to begin.

parts.title: Keeping Your Insides Inside
parts.blurb: Bleeding, wounds, bones, burns, and the restraint that keeps care useful.

parts.title: The Less Cinematic Ways to Die
parts.blurb: Water, weather, feet and the illnesses that did not read the script.

parts.title: The Pharmacy Has Stopped Answering
parts.blurb: Useful supplies, honest storage and the prescription that belongs to a person.

parts.title: Someone Has to Do the Nursing
parts.blurb: The hours after the rescue, the people a standard plan forgets, and room to rest.

parts.title: Read This When Your Brain Has Left
parts.blurb: Reminders and records for the next person through the door.

captions: The doorway is not a treatment area until the roof has agreed.
Practise on the mannequin. It has excellent patience and no rib-related opinions.
An orderly queue is useful. A colour is not a diagnosis.
The teddy has requested a dressing proportionate to the imaginary injury.
Soap: the unglamorous recruit with the best attendance record.
Support the person. Decline the chair if it requires a second rescue team.
The kettle remains a kitchen appliance, however dramatic the circumstances.
Clean and dirty are separate departments. They do not share a bucket.
Dry socks have done more for morale than several inspirational speeches.
The dental department opens every morning, preferably before trouble does.
Useful supplies are welcome. The crystal has been referred to the decorations committee.
Cool, dry and labelled: three qualities the cupboard must possess in reality.
The treatment plan belongs to the person whose name is on it.
The rescue is over. The care is not.
An accessible table is an excellent place to begin civilisation again.
Sometimes the useful intervention is a blanket, a quiet voice and time.
Leave the next person a kit they can find and a record they can read.
alt: A bespectacled survivor stops friendly zombies entering a damaged cottage; one carries an oversized satchel.
The survivor and puzzled zombies sit beside a CPR training mannequin and an unused defibrillator case.
A calm fictional aid station with seated green zombies and plain coloured pennants.
A clean training table with dressings, gloves and unused tourniquets beside a large teddy bear.
The survivor washes hands with soap while a zombie offers a watering can of daisies.
A survivor in an arm sling rests in a meadow while a friendly zombie carries a wooden chair.
A cottage washroom with a clean basin and kettle safely on a high shelf.
A sunny outdoor drinking-water and handwashing station with covered containers.
A cottage porch in cold rain with drying socks and a blanket around a friendly zombie.
The survivor and zombies brush their teeth beside a basin.
The survivor organises sealed medical supplies while a zombie offers a decorative crystal.
A dry pantry shelf holds a thermometer, insulated carrier and original medicine cartons.
An older woman and the survivor organise closed medicine boxes and a personal notebook.
The survivor offers a drink in a tidy makeshift ward while a zombie sweeps.
A parent, child, wheelchair user and survivor meet at an accessible table.
The survivor and a blanket-wrapped zombie sit quietly together in a peaceful dusk garden.
A dawn teaching table with clean supplies and a notebook, attended by the survivor and zombies.
